note: `text` is the caption shown in subtitles; `say` (optional) is a phonetic spelling fed to the TTS engine. `pause` is extra silence after the line, in seconds.

lines.text: It always rains in this town.
And somewhere out there, a story is looking for its next case.
This is SCP-3143: Murphy Law in… The Foundation Always Rings Twice!
lines.say: This is S C P, thirty-one forty-three. Murphy Law in... The Foundation Always Rings Twice!

lines.text: A Euclid-class anomaly from the SCP Wiki, written by The Great Hippo.
lines.say: A Euclid-class anomaly from the S C P Wiki, written by The Great Hippo.

lines.text: SCP-3143 is an intrafictional construct: a living, thinking story that can warp reality.
lines.say: S C P thirty-one forty-three is an intra-fictional construct. A living, thinking story, that can warp reality.

lines.text: When it activates, it flattens part of the real world into a movie script: a hard-boiled crime noir, straight out of the 1930s.
lines.say: When it activates, it flattens part of the real world into a movie script. A hard-boiled crime noir, straight out of the nineteen-thirties.

lines.text: Inside that script, SCP-3143 plays the lead: a private detective hired to crack a case.
lines.say: Inside that script, S C P thirty-one forty-three plays the lead. A private detective, hired to crack a case.

lines.text: Anyone caught in the effect becomes a character, talking and acting like they walked out of a pulp novel.
The story runs until the case is solved the way the genre demands. Then reality snaps back.
Whatever happened in the story really happened. But the people involved usually remember none of it.
The detective's name? Murphy Law.
It's a pun on Murphy's Law: anything that can go wrong, will.
Containing a story isn't easy.
A Foundation bot called I/O-ISMETA scans online fiction communities for signs that Murphy is back.
lines.say: A Foundation bot named I O Iz-meta scans online fiction communities for signs that Murphy is back.

lines.text: When he surfaces, a member of the Pataphysics Department, experts in the logic of fiction, is sent to deconstruct him.
lines.say: When he surfaces, a member of the Pataphysics Department, experts in the logic of fiction, is sent to deconstruct him.

lines.text: And Mobile Task Force Iota-10, the "Damn Freds," hunts for SCP-3143-A: the man who wrote him.
lines.say: And Mobile Task Force Iota Ten, the Damn Freds, hunts for S C P thirty-one forty-three A. The man who wrote him.

lines.text: SCP-3143 was first noticed in 2005, after a containment breach at Site-95.
lines.say: S C P thirty-one forty-three was first noticed in two thousand five, after a containment breach at Site ninety-five.

lines.text: In 2012, the Pataphysics Department and the Department of Analytics finally made contact.
lines.say: In twenty twelve, the Pataphysics Department and the Department of Analytics finally made contact.

lines.text: In Interview 001, Dr. Thaddeus Thaum, a literature expert from the Pataphysics Department, walks into Murphy's office.
lines.say: In interview zero zero one, Doctor Thaddeus Thawm, a literature expert from the Pataphysics Department, walks into Murphy's office.

lines.text: Murphy narrates, draws his .44… and Thaum calmly points out that he can hear the narration.
lines.say: Murphy narrates, draws his forty-four... and Thawm calmly points out, that he can hear the narration.

lines.text: Then Thaum critiques the story to pieces. It isn't even proper noir, he says. No doomed anti-hero. No moral grey.
lines.say: Then Thawm critiques the story to pieces. It isn't even proper noir, he says. No doomed anti-hero. No moral grey.

lines.text: Just "fantasy escapism dressed up in a suit, a hat, and a drinking habit."
lines.say: Just fantasy escapism, dressed up in a suit, a hat, and a drinking habit.

lines.text: As the critique lands, the screenplay collapses into a plain transcript, and Murphy is gone.
In his place sits SCP-3143-A: Murphy Lawden, a retired shoe salesman from New Jersey who lives alone with two cats.
lines.say: In his place sits S C P thirty-one forty-three A. Murphy Lawden, a retired shoe salesman from New Jersey, who lives alone with two cats.

lines.text: Years ago, he wrote an unfinished screenplay called It Always Rains.
The next day, Lawden asks the question every writer dreads: was the script any good?
"It was fairly awful."
lines.say: It was. Fairly awful.

lines.text: By Interview 018, Lawden is miserable. He's stopped eating, and his pencils have been taken away, because he keeps writing about Murphy.
lines.say: By interview zero one eight, Lawden is miserable. He's stopped eating, and his pencils have been taken away, because he keeps writing about Murphy.

lines.text: Why did the story have to stop? Murphy was helping people. It was fun.
Then he turns the tables. The Foundation, he says, cloaks itself in the trappings of science: the terms, the titles, the interview logs.
All to make its own story sound plausible.
The transcript snaps back into a screenplay. The subject isn't Lawden anymore. It's Murphy.
And he has a line for all of us: we're all just characters in that trashy dime-store novel called life.
He tosses Thaum aside, lights a cigarette, and walks out.
lines.say: He tosses Thawm aside, lights a cigarette, and walks out.

lines.text: Then comes the twist, locked behind Level 4 clearance.
lines.say: Then comes the twist. Locked behind level four clearance.

lines.text: In an email, Site Director August admits that Dr. Thaum and the Pataphysics Department were made up: a test run for a fictional countermeasure.
lines.say: In an email, Site Director August admits that Doctor Thawm, and the Pataphysics Department, were made up. A test run for a fictional countermeasure.

lines.text: Even Murphy Lawden and It Always Rains never existed.
The Foundation tried to beat a story by writing a better one… and it didn't work.
lines.say: The Foundation tried to beat a story, by writing a better one... and it didn't work.

lines.text: August orders everyone to leave SCP-3143 alone. They've learned a lot about him, but he's learned a lot about them, too.
lines.say: August orders everyone to leave S C P thirty-one forty-three alone. They've learned a lot about him. But he's learned a lot about them, too.

lines.text: And one more thing: SCP-423, a creature that slips itself into written stories, has gone missing.
lines.say: And one more thing. S C P four twenty-three, a creature that slips itself into written stories, has gone missing.

lines.text: Then, just like a movie, the file ends with credits.
Dr. Thaum, played by Thaddeus Thaum. The task force, played by Fred.
lines.say: Doctor Thawm, played by Thaddeus Thawm. The task force, played by Fred.

lines.text: And Murphy Law… played by himself.
lines.say: And Murphy Law... played by himself.

lines.text: So, what is SCP-3143?
lines.say: So, what is S C P thirty-one forty-three?

lines.text: A detective who knows he's fictional, and suspects that you are, too.
Every attempt to contain him is just another story. And Murphy Law is very good at stories.
